# Render an image

<!-- Generated by examples/manual_steps.rs from the app's own menu, space, editor and status sets. Do not edit by hand. -->

<link rel="stylesheet" href="theme.css">

## 1. Render ▸ Render Image

![Render ▸ Render Image](render-an-image/01-render-render-image.svg)

Open Render in the top bar and choose Render Image — or press F12 anywhere.

## 2. The render takes the viewport's area

![The render takes the viewport's area](render-an-image/02-the-render-takes-the-viewport-s-area.svg)

The area turns into the Image editor on Render Result. The line across it reads Frame, Time, Remaining, Mem and Sample as Blender's does.

## 3. The status bar carries the render

![The status bar carries the render](render-an-image/03-the-status-bar-carries-the-render.svg)

Its progress and an X to cancel (Esc does the same), then the render as one button: Status, Sample, Time, Remaining.

## 4. Click it to see the whole event

![Click it to see the whole event](render-an-image/04-click-it-to-see-the-whole-event.svg)

The Outliner turns to its Status mode: what the render was asked for, the settings it was given, and how it ended.

## 5. Image ▸ Save As

![Image ▸ Save As](render-an-image/05-image-save-as.svg)

Open the Image editor's Image menu and choose Save As… (Shift Alt S).

## 6. Name the file and save

![Name the file and save](render-an-image/06-name-the-file-and-save.svg)

The file browser opens over the window. Type a name and press the button to write the render.

## 7. Esc gives the area back

![Esc gives the area back](render-an-image/07-esc-gives-the-area-back.svg)

Esc (or F11, View Render) returns the area to the editor it was before the render.
